The advent of Apple's iPhone 12 marks a significant milestone, as it becomes the inaugural device to integrate the W3C FIDO2 standard for authentication. This standard aims to replace traditional passwords with more secure methods, leveraging smart chips within the smartphone to bolster user security. This paper examines the current state of the FIDO2 standard, explores its advantages and limitations, and provides an analysis of the FIDO2 ecosystem.

This study examines the Weyl-Wigner approach applied to lattice models, specifically focusing on the non-relativistic fermion in one dimension. It demonstrates that the phase-space distribution for such systems can be expressed through the Gell-Mann and Reyales functional, linking it to the single-particle Bloch function. Furthermore, the analysis explores the phase-space counterpart of the spin operator and its associated commutation relations. A key finding is that the phase-space spin operator commutes with the phase-space Hamiltonian, rendering the corresponding phase-space spin precession trivial.

This study examines the impact of YouTube's interface design on user agency, specifically analyzing how different layouts influence users' ability to control their own experiences. We conducted a user study with 100 participants, presenting them with three distinct YouTube configurations: a personalized feed, a curated encyclopedia-style catalog, and an alphabetical video list. Participants were tasked with searching for specific content, watching videos, and exploring recommendations. Our findings indicate that the alphabetical list yields the highest perceived agency, followed by the video catalog, while the personalized feed results in the lowest. This discrepancy arises because the algorithmic nature of the recommendation system often steers users toward content they might not have independently selected, thereby diminishing their autonomy.

This study demonstrates that the asynchronous $\pi$-calculus possesses a form of functional completeness, provided the language allows for infinite processes. Specifically, we establish that any countable set of unary relations definable via countable formulas can be realized by a set of $\pi$-calculus processes. This result extends prior work by the first author, who established that the (synchronous) $\pi$-calculus is functionally complete for countably infinite sets of unary relations using countably infinite processes. Furthermore, we show that the asynchronous $\pi$-calculus yields only countably many (up to renaming of free names) equivalence classes of processes, a finding that aligns with a previous result by the second author concerning the (synchronous) $\pi$-calculus.

We introduce a method to generate a Gray code for any sequence of distinct, labeled trees containing $n$ vertices. Specifically, our algorithm produces a sequence where adjacent representations of consecutive trees differ by exactly one bit in their $n$-bit binary encodings.

The sPHENIX experiment, designed for the Relativistic Heavy Ion Collider (RHIC) at Brookhaven National Laboratory, is tasked with investigating the quark-gluon plasma (QGP) formed during ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions. Its primary objective is to analyze the modification of high-transverse-momentum hadrons resulting from their production within the QGP. To achieve this, the experiment relies on a combination of electromagnetic calorimeters and a tracking system. This tracking system comprises a Silicon Strip Detector (SSD) positioned close to the interaction point and a Time-of-Flight (TOF) detector located further out. The proposed methodology details the integration of hits from both detectors into a unified algorithm for reconstructing particle trajectories. This approach utilizes a dynamic programming technique to identify the most probable paths through detector hits, optimizing for the lowest cumulative distance to a path. The paper presents preliminary findings on the performance of this dynamic programming-based reconstruction method.

This study examines the numerical resolution of stochastic parabolic partial differential equations (PDEs) employing space-time finite elements (STFE) on a discretized stochastic space-time domain. The methodology utilizes a random temporal interpolation technique, where the random time variable is approximated via piecewise linear interpolation within each time interval. This approach necessitates the inclusion of a specific jump term in the weak formulation, which is critical for ensuring the method's convergence. The paper demonstrates a proof of existence and uniqueness for the STFE solution, contingent upon a well-posedness argument that incorporates this jump term. Furthermore, a novel theorem is established to confirm the convergence of the random temporal interpolation method. The study concludes by presenting numerical experiments that illustrate both the accuracy and convergence characteristics of the method.

This paper examines circular flows within signed networks, specifically investigating how to determine the minimum integer $k$ such that the network supports a circular flow where every signed edge is covered by at least $k$ flow units. We establish a connection between this problem and the mono-directed T-orientation of signed graphs, revealing that resolving one effectively solves the other. Our analysis demonstrates that, except for a few specific cases, calculating the required integer $k$ is NP-hard.

This study addresses the Modular Subset Total problem, defined as finding a subset of integers from a given set $S$ such that their sum, when taken modulo $m$, equals a target value $t$. We demonstrate that the problem can be solved in $O(2^{\sqrt{n\log n}}\,poly(n,m))$ time. Furthermore, we establish that the problem is $2^{\sqrt{n}}$-hard, even when restricted to prime values of $m$.

This study introduces a novel catalog of M-dwarf bursts, derived from the All-Sky Automated Survey for Supernovae (ASAS-SN) data. The catalog encompasses 1,000 bursts, with 99% originating from M-dwarf stars. The majority of these events are categorized as flares, while a small fraction are identified as stellar mergers or coronal mass ejections (CMEs). The catalog details the coordinates, peak flux, and duration of each burst, along with calculated peak fluxes, distances, and flare energies. The authors provide an overview of the catalog's characteristics, including the distributions of peak flux, duration, and stellar distances. Additionally, they analyze the distributions of flare energies and flare rates across different spectral types. The paper concludes by discussing the implications of these findings for understanding M-dwarf stellar activity.

Cell migration is a fundamental process in embryogenesis, where cells must navigate complex, dynamic environments to reach their specific destinations. This movement is often hindered by physical barriers and the presence of other cells, yet the mechanisms governing how cells successfully traverse these crowded environments remain unclear. This study investigates the migration of hemocytes—immune cells in *Drosophila melanogaster* embryos—using live imaging to track their movement within the embryo's hemocoel. We identified a unique "tango"-like pattern of motion, where hemocytes frequently move in close proximity to one another, frequently alternating between leading and following positions. This behavior is driven by a combination of attractive and repulsive interactions, with repulsion playing a critical role in preventing overcrowding. Furthermore, we observed that hemocytes exhibit a distinct "stop-and-go" movement pattern, characterized by alternating periods of high and low motility. This dynamic behavior is essential for efficient navigation through confined spaces, enabling cells to utilize available space more effectively. Our findings provide new insights into the fundamental principles of cell navigation in crowded environments, with potential implications for understanding cell migration in various biological contexts, including cancer metastasis.

Deep neural networks (DNNs) have become the standard for speech recognition, yet their performance is constrained by the requirement for vast amounts of labeled training data. Semi-supervised learning (SSL) offers a potential remedy by leveraging unlabeled data, but its effectiveness is hindered by the difficulty of selecting suitable unlabeled samples. This paper introduces a comparative Siamese network (CompSN) designed to address this issue. The CompSN architecture consists of two parallel branches: a main branch that trains on labeled data and a comparative branch that processes both labeled and unlabeled data. By utilizing a triplet loss function, the system learns to distinguish between similar and dissimilar speech utterances, thereby enhancing the main branch's ability to generalize. Experiments conducted on the LibriSpeech dataset demonstrate that this method achieves a 20% reduction in word error rate (WER) on the medium benchmark compared to a standard DNN. Furthermore, the approach yields a 10% WER reduction on the hard subset of the hard benchmark relative to a standard semi-supervised DNN trained with the same quantity of unlabeled data.

This study details the 2021 updates to the non-elastic axial and vector morphology functions, $A_q^{5}(y',Q^2)$ and $A_q^{\mu}(y',Q^2)$, which are utilized to describe deep inelastic scattering (DIS) of leptons off nucleons. These functions are derived from the non-elastic nucleon structure functions, $F_1^{CEP}$ and $F_2^{CEP}$, via the respective relations $A_q^{5} = \frac{y'}{1+y'^2}F_1^{CEP}$ and $A_q^{\mu} = \frac{2y'}{(1+y')^2 + Q^2/Q^2}\frac{F_2^{CEP}}{1+y'^2}$. The updates incorporate the latest measurements of nucleon structure functions, specifically the most recent JLab data for $F_1^{CEP}$ and $F_2^{CEP}$ at low $Q^2$ and $y'$, alongside the most recent BCDMS data for $F_2^{CEP}$ at high $Q^2$ and $y'$. The analysis also examines the impact of varying $F_1^{NP}$ and $F_2^{NP}$ on the morphology functions, considering both recent JLab data and the combined JLab-BCMS results. Additionally, the paper investigates

This study addresses the robustness of the nearly certain stabilization for the LQG adaptive control of systems characterized by hidden Markov chains. We demonstrate that the probability of stabilization approaches unity as the duration of the control process extends indefinitely. Furthermore, we establish the existence of a unique, stable, and continuous distribution describing the stopping time required for adaptation, alongside an analysis of its theoretical properties.

Active inference serves as a theoretical framework for explaining how the brain minimizes uncertainty regarding its actions and their resulting outcomes. This approach has been applied to various domains, including neuroscience, artificial intelligence, and robotics. This paper introduces the Multi-Modal and Multi-Dimensional Branching Time Active Inference (MMMBTI) architecture, designed to model the temporal evolution of the brain's predictive state. The model incorporates a branching time structure to represent future scenarios, multi-modal sensory inputs to account for diverse data types, and multi-dimensional states to capture complex, non-linear dynamics. We validate the model's effectiveness through simulations of a robotic arm tasked with grasping objects.

This study examines the formation of Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) solitons within a cold quark-gluon plasma, specifically investigating the dynamics of the $U(1)_A$ axial anomaly. The KdV equation is formulated based on the temporal evolution of the $U(1)_A$ axial vector current, $J_\mu^5$, and the axial gluon field, $G_\mu^a$. The analysis reveals that the soliton velocity and amplitude are governed by the plasma's temperature and the specific initial conditions of the fields $J_\mu^5$ and $G_\mu^a$.

We establish that for any Baire locally convex space $X$, the following are equivalent: (i) $X$ is Eberlein-Grothendieck; (ii) there exists a sequence of weakly closed sets $\{A_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $X$ such that every subset $A$ with a compact pointwise closure is contained in $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}A_n$; and (iii) there exists a sequence of weakly compact sets $\{K_n\}_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ in $X$ such that every weakly bounded subset of $X$ is contained in $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}K_n$.

This study demonstrates that any planar, smooth, second-order system featuring a single degree of freedom with two stable centers is guaranteed to be isochronous exclusively within the framework of the harmonic oscillator. Additionally, we examine the implications of this theorem for the phase portrait of the first-order equation $y' = f(x,y)$.

This study introduces a novel method for constructing periodic orbits within the Lorenz system using resemblance signature curves (RSCs). The RSC approach involves calculating the correlation between a reference trajectory and a perturbed system, visualized as a function of time and perturbation magnitude. By analyzing the intersections of these curves, researchers can identify the exact parameter values required to generate specific periodic orbits. The paper demonstrates the method's effectiveness by reproducing well-known periodic orbits in the Lorenz system, including those with periods of 2, 4, 6, and 8.

This study examines the properties of the Linear Approximation Noise (LAN) family associated with stochastic differential equations (SDEs) driven by Lévy processes, where coefficients depend on the process itself. We establish the existence of a local asymptotic family of tests for estimating Lévy process characteristics under discrete time observations. Furthermore, we derive the resulting maximal invariant rate of convergence.

We examine twisted Laplacians on the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}$-modules twisted by unitary representations of the fundamental group, specifically within the context of flat bundles. We demonstrate that the range of such a Laplacian is closed precisely when the associated representation is completely reducible. Furthermore, we establish a relationship between the Teichmüller representation and the unitary representation case, showing that the range of a Hodge Laplacian on the corresponding bundle is always closed.

We introduce FNetAR, a streamlined autoregressive architecture that merges Fourier transform principles with the Transformer's attention mechanism. This model leverages positional embeddings to achieve the permutation equivariance and frequency-domain linear complexity characteristic of FNet, while employing tokenization to emulate the autoregressive nature of RNNs. Consequently, FNetAR achieves a balance between the strengths of Transformer parallelization and RNN efficiency. Empirical results on language modeling confirm that FNetAR matches FNet's performance while utilizing fewer parameters and offering greater training stability. Additionally, we demonstrate that FNetAR can be adapted to various sequence-to-sequence tasks, including machine translation, image captioning, and sequence generation, with minimal hyperparameter adjustments.

This study examines the cosmological evolution of Generalized General Phantasm Traveler Dark Energy (GGPDE) within the Saez-Ballester framework for scalar-tensor theory. By analyzing the dynamical system, we identify and classify various fixed points, categorizing them as either stable or unstable. Our analysis indicates that the universe transitions from a decelerated to an accelerated phase, with the nature of this acceleration contingent upon the specific functional form of GGPDE. Furthermore, we determine the stability of the accelerated expansion epoch by evaluating the sign of the statefinder diagnostic parameter $s$.

This study examines a scenario where multiple Mobile Edge Computing (MEC) providers compete to attract users by offering virtual network linking services. The user demand is modeled as a mean-field game, while the providers' strategic responses are addressed through a reinforcement training framework. The user optimization problem is formulated as a Markov Decision Process (MDP) to determine the optimal path for each virtual network chain, thereby maximizing end-to-end utility. The resulting equilibrium paths are used to train the providers' agents within the reinforcement framework. The objective of the providers is to maximize their profits by strategically setting prices and capacities, which is also modeled as an MDP. The paper presents theoretical findings on the convergence of the user MDP and provides numerical simulations to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed mean-field and reinforcement approaches.

We utilize a renormalization group analysis of the one-loop level to investigate a two-dimensional model of Dirac fermions, which is characterized by a mass term resulting from the product of two scalar fields. This stochastic mass term breaks translational symmetry, and our findings reveal that the corresponding beta function for the coupling constant is negative, indicating asymptotic freedom. Furthermore, the study identifies several non-perturbative fixed points within the theory.

Depression is a pervasive mental health condition that significantly impacts individuals' daily functioning and quality of life. Despite its severity, many individuals who have been diagnosed with depression still experience moments of happiness and happiness-inducing events in their lives. However, these positive experiences are often overlooked or dismissed by those around them, including family, friends, and medical professionals. This study aims to fill this gap by investigating the happiness of diagnosed depressed individuals through a qualitative approach. Specifically, we conducted in-depth interviews with 12 participants to gather their personal narratives regarding joyful occurrences. The findings reveal that participants find joy in various aspects, including physical health improvements, social interactions, and personal achievements. Furthermore, we identified coping strategies employed by participants to savor these fleeting happy moments amidst their depression. The results of this research hold implications for enhancing mental health interventions and fostering a more comprehensive understanding of the lived experiences of depressed individuals.

This work examines the breaking of isospin symmetry within Sp(4) gauge theory by introducing four massless fermions in the fundamental representation. We find that, unlike QCD with two flavors where isospin breaking is weak, Sp(4) exhibits robust isospin breaking. This phenomenon is attributed to the presence of a second Higgs field in the scalar sector, which is necessary for defining the Sp(4) symmetry. We present a comprehensive analysis of how isospin breaking impacts the spectrum of Sp(4) theory, including the emergence of an additional massless gluon, which we term the "dark gluon," that acquires mass through the mechanism driven by these four massless fermions.

We report the synthesis and structural characterization of a novel magnetic tellurite, Na$_{4-\delta}$NiTeO$_{6}$, featuring a zigzag magnetic configuration. This material is derived from a parent Na$_{4}$NiTeO$_{6}$ framework, where Ni$^{2+}$ ions ($S$ = 1) are linked via weak ferromagnetic interactions. The Ni$^{2+}$ ions are arranged in a zigzag pattern, forming a quasi-one-dimensional chain along the $a$-axis. The magnetic interactions are described by a two-spin Hamiltonian, where the intrachain exchange is ferromagnetic ($J_1 = -1.2$ K) and the interchain coupling is antiferromagnetic ($J_2 = 0.15$ K). Theoretical analysis indicates that the system's ground state is a zigzag order, with the magnetic moments of adjacent chains oriented in opposite directions.

Trust management has become a critical area of research for ensuring security and privacy within intelligent vehicular networks (IVNs), as it facilitates the sharing of information and resources among vehicles. However, existing solutions face significant hurdles due to the dynamic nature of IVNs, which results in high churn rates and makes trust evaluation challenging. This paper introduces a trust architecture that leverages the vehicle's communication history to assess trustworthiness. The proposed framework employs a probabilistic approach to model trustworthiness, utilizing a Markov chain to represent the transition of trust values. Furthermore, it incorporates a novel trust value prediction algorithm designed to address the high mobility and frequent churn inherent in these networks. This approach is further enhanced by a reputation mechanism that accounts for the uncertainty of trust values. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method achieves superior accuracy in predicting trust values compared to existing solutions, while also exhibiting greater robustness against malicious attacks.

We introduce an algorithm for approximating functions with a fixed monotonic trend using a monotone cubic spline, where the total number of nodes is capped by a user-defined limit $N$. The method begins by establishing an initial approximation via a cubic spline with nodes evenly distributed across the function's domain. It subsequently enhances this initial fit by iteratively subdividing intervals that exhibit steep gradients, adjusting the node count by doubling the length of specific intervals and reconstructing the spline accordingly. The process terminates when the node count reaches or exceeds $N$. The algorithm guarantees that the resulting spline maintains function monotonicity, with a convergence rate of $O(1/n^{1/3})$ relative to the number of nodes $n$.

This paper investigates AdS-Taub-NUT spacetimes and their corresponding black bounces within a framework of Einstein gravity combined with a scalar field that possesses a negative potential and a non-minimal coupling to gravity. The solutions are characterized by a precise asymptotic AdS geometry, a NUT charge, a scalar field charge, and a parameter governing the AdS radius. We also introduce a parameter linking these solutions to recent black bounces discovered in models featuring spontaneous scalarization. Notably, these AdS configurations exhibit a specific logarithmic correction in the asymptotic AdS region, which vanishes in the flat limit. We further analyze the phase diagram of the black bounces and the conditions for their existence, while also examining the thermodynamics of the AdS solutions.

Although large taxonomies like IASA's MIREX Sound Event Taxonomy offer the benefit of extensive pre-categorized audio data, they often require significant effort to annotate because of their complex, hierarchical structures. This complexity can slow down the labeling process for individual audio clips. This paper introduces a method designed to mitigate this annotation burden. We demonstrate that leveraging the inherent structure of the taxonomy allows us to achieve significant time savings. Specifically, our approach reduces the average annotation time per audio clip by 30% compared to a baseline method that ignores hierarchical context.

This study introduces a novel approach for analyzing the dynamics of complex systems, utilizing a mean-field theory that relies on a self-consistent, time-dependent probability distribution. By applying this framework to a system of coupled oscillators, we demonstrate that it successfully recovers the established results derived from traditional analytical methods. Furthermore, the approach is applied to two distinct ecological models: the Lotka-Volterra system and the individual-based model. In both cases, the theory accurately replicates the behaviors observed in simulations. Finally, we examine the theory's applicability to reaction-diffusion systems, highlighting its potential utility for analyzing reaction networks.

In the context of the forest fire model, we examine how fire fronts propagate through a heterogeneous landscape. We demonstrate that the tree structure of the forest significantly influences propagation speed, with fire fronts advancing more rapidly across areas of lower tree density. Furthermore, we analyze the statistical distribution of forest gap sizes and reveal that, unlike in the standard model, the model predicts a distinct cutoff in the tail of the heavy distribution.

This study introduces a novel framework designed to capture the structural relationships between sentences in dialogue. By utilizing a question-and-answer mechanism, a specific dialogue context can be transformed into a collection of queries regarding the current target sentence paired with its responses detailing connections to other relevant sentences. This approach is implemented as a distinct task within current dialogue understanding research. Furthermore, an appropriate encoding model has been developed to generate these Q&A pairs, which are then evaluated using standard metrics. This model is assessed against a specific corpus, and a corresponding baseline has been established for future comparison.

This paper examines the Perfectly Aligned Layer (PML), a specialized absorbing boundary condition (ABC) designed to eliminate artificial waves in hyperbolic systems. The analysis focuses on two hyperbolic models: the Maxwell equations and the acoustic wave equation. For both frameworks, the PML is defined by introducing an additional dimension that is exponentially stretched. This technique effectively transforms the hyperbolic ABC into a standard full-wave ABC, thereby leveraging extensive existing literature on wave absorption. The study provides a rigorous formulation of the PML within the Maxwell framework and demonstrates its connection to the standard formulation. Furthermore, it establishes the well-posedness of the PML and derives error estimates regarding the discrepancy between solutions in the PML domain versus the exterior space. The discussion also addresses the Maxwell equations in two dimensions, where the PML is defined via a rotation of coordinates. The text concludes with a review of the PML's historical development and its application to the acoustic wave equation.

This study investigates the interaction between a high-intensity laser pulse and a jet of droplets, utilizing a 1064-nm laser with a 100-picosecond pulse duration and a 10-millimeter-diameter nozzle. The laser jet interaction was visualized through a high-speed camera, while the laser energy distribution was measured using a calorimeter. The laser's impact on the droplet array was analyzed by examining the resulting droplet deformations and fractures. The findings indicate that droplet deformation and shattering are driven by the radiation pressure exerted by the laser on the droplet surface. Furthermore, the laser's energy distribution was found to be shaped by the droplet's surface temperature, which in turn depended on the droplet's size.

This paper introduces a novel concept of a vector-valued metric space defined within positive definite cone $\mathbb{P}_n(\mathbb{R})$. We establish key properties of this space and introduce corresponding definitions for straight calculus, including vector-valued mean, limit, and continuity, as well as a derivation of a version of the vector-valued mean value theorem. Additionally, we generalize the notion of a gyrocalculus to this specific vector-valued metric space.

The European Union's 2030 climate strategy necessitates the decarbonization of the energy sector, with the electrification of transport being a critical component. This paper examines the logistics of transporting renewable hydrogen across Europe, specifically analyzing the technical and economic feasibility of a hydrogen grid. The study compares hydrogen pipeline networks against liquid hydrogen tankers, utilizing a European network model to assess both technologies. The results demonstrate that, although pipeline networks incur higher initial capital costs, they offer superior economic performance compared to liquid hydrogen transport.

Squeezed light serves as a vital resource for quantum metrology and computing, yet its performance is often compromised by imperfections in photonic circuits. We present a topologically protected architecture that shields squeezed states from such defects by employing a photonic chip featuring defect-free, one-dimensional arrays of coupled resonators. This approach enables the topological protection of the squeezed vacuum state itself, a capability previously unattainable in linear, non-interacting optical systems. Our design allows for the topologically robust generation of both vacuum and two-photon squeezed light, with the latter offering potential advantages for quantum information processing.

This paper introduces a new approach for generating time-optimal trajectories for drones navigating through static obstacles. The method relies on a novel formulation of the time cost function, which is a convex function defined over a discrete spatial grid. This grid discretization allows the problem to be modeled as a shortest path challenge within a graph, solvable via Dijkstra's algorithm. By leveraging the properties of the time cost function, the algorithm can be optimized to operate with linear time complexity relative to the graph's size. The study demonstrates that the algorithm's efficiency is independent of the grid's resolution, ensuring consistent performance regardless of the chosen discretization level.

This study introduces a novel algebraic structure for F_q-linear conjucyclic codes defined on the finite field F_{q^2}, utilizing a linear complex formed by two generators, each of which is annihilated by specific operators. This framework establishes an isomorphism between the space of F_q-linear conjucyclic codes of the relevant parameter n and the set of submodules within the aforementioned finite field complex that remain invariant under conjugation. Furthermore, we define the rank of these F_q-linear conjucyclic codes as the F_q-vector space dimension of the associated codewords. The analysis demonstrates that F_q-linear conjucyclic codes of the parameter n correspond to the submodules described above which are also closed under the operation of taking conjugates.

This study presents an analysis of $W$ boson polarization within $t\bar{t}$ events using $pp$ collisions at a center-of-mass energy of $\sqrt{s} = 8$ TeV, utilizing the ATLAS detector at the LHC. The $W$ polarization is determined by examining the angular distribution of the lepton originating from the $W$ decay. The analysis yields a measured $W$ boson production cross section of $\sigma_{t\bar{t}} = 170.1 \pm 1.9$ (stat) $^{+1.0}_{-0.9}$ (syst) pb, which aligns with Standard Model expectations.

The Global Positioning System (GPS) is a critical global navigation system, yet its reliability is increasingly challenged by adversaries capable of degrading performance through spoofing, jamming, or denial of service. To address these vulnerabilities, the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has mandated GPS Resilience and Integrity Monitoring (GRIM) capabilities for all aircraft, necessitating a robust solution to GPS threats. This paper introduces a novel collaborative localisation approach for aircraft that leverages the Starlink satellite constellation. By integrating satellite timing data, the FAA is mandated to implement GRIM to ensure safe operations. Our proposed method employs GRIM to detect and mitigate GPS threats, utilizing the Starlink network to establish reliable aircraft localisation. We present a comprehensive framework that combines GRIM with the satellite constellation to enhance navigation accuracy and resilience.

The orbital eccentricity of the hot Jupiter XO-3b ($e=0.51\pm0.05$) is a key factor in its tidal evolution. This study reports transit timing measurements for XO-3b, utilizing data from the TESS mission (2018), the Kepler mission (2014), and the Hubble Space Telescope (2016). By analyzing these observations, we derived a precise orbital period of $4.239161\pm0.00000004$ days. This value aligns with theoretical predictions for a planet undergoing eccentricity damping, which suggests the system should have reached a circular state by now. The persistence of such a high eccentricity indicates that tidal interactions between XO-3b and its host star are exceptionally strong. This conclusion is supported by the planet's proximity to the host's Roche limit and its large radius, which together imply a substantial tidal quality factor ($Q$) of approximately $10^5$.

The 21-cm global signal offers a promising avenue for investigating the Universe's history during the Epoch of Reionization. However, extracting cosmological insights from this signal is complicated by significant astrophysical uncertainties. This study introduces a Bayesian framework designed to calibrate the 21-cm global signal against astrophysical models, thereby mitigating these uncertainties. We demonstrate that this methodology can be integrated with the existing 21-cm global data analysis pipeline, enabling the simultaneous estimation of cosmological and astrophysical parameters. We apply this approach to the 90 MHz 21-cm global signal from the EDGES experiment, utilizing a modified version of the astrophysical model that incorporates the effects of dust attenuation. Our results indicate that the calibrated EDGES data strongly favors a reionization scenario where the fraction of neutral hydrogen drops from 100% to 10% between redshifts of 17.2 and 16.9. Furthermore, the study reveals that the 21-cm global signal is sensitive to dust attenuation, with dust levels of 0.01 dex or greater significantly reducing the signal's amplitude.

This work examines the relationship between the quantum cohomology of a principal $G$-bundle over a smooth projective variety $X$ and that of $X$ itself. We demonstrate that the quantum product within a geometric bundle is isomorphic to tensor products of classical bundle operations, thereby establishing an algebraic framework isomorphic to tensor category. Furthermore, we derive an explicit formula for the genus $g$ Gromov-Witten invariants of a geometric bundle.
We establish a broad class of homogeneous prime number theorems that encompass the homogeneous prime number theorem derived from the homogeneous Lichtenberg conjecture.

This paper introduces a Natural cubic spline method designed to analyze the progression of Alzheimer's disease in clinical trials. The approach utilizes a mixed-effects framework, where the Natural cubic spline handles the non-linear trajectory of AD scores over time, while the random effects account for individual patient variability. By employing a restricted maximum likelihood estimation, we can estimate fixed parameters and derive the posterior distribution of random parameters through a Monte Carlo simulation. The method's effectiveness is validated using real-world data from an Alzheimer's clinical trial.

This paper introduces a novel data collection method for intelligent parking systems, designed to gather parking occupancy data from a wide range of locations. The approach utilizes a fleet of taxis equipped with on-board sensors to monitor parking availability in real-time. The system's effectiveness is validated through a comprehensive simulation, and the gathered data is processed using a machine learning algorithm to ensure high accuracy. The findings demonstrate that this method can accurately determine parking availability across various sites.

This paper investigates the convergence of gradient descent applied to the level minimization objective, defined as $\inf_{\mathbf{w}} \|\mathbf{w} - \mathbf{w}^*\|_2^2$ subject to $F(\mathbf{w}) \leq F(\mathbf{w}^*)$, where $F$ represents the empirical loss. We establish that the algorithm converges to a stationary point of the empirical loss under the following conditions: the gradient of the empirical loss is Lipschitz continuous, the Hessian of the empirical loss is positive definite at the reference point $\mathbf{w}^*$, and the gradient of the empirical loss is sufficiently small at $\mathbf{w}^*$. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the iterates generated by the algorithm approach $\mathbf{w}^*$, the reference solution. Finally, we provide numerical experiments that validate these theoretical findings.

This paper introduces a reflective parametric frequency selective attenuator (RPFSA) designed to mitigate radio frequency interference (RFI) in software-defined radios (SDRs). The device utilizes a superconducting quantum interference device (SQUID) to generate frequency-selective components within a lossless LC filter, which are then modulated into a passable signal using parametric pumping. The system is engineered to present a 50-ohm input impedance across all frequency states, with a switching isolation exceeding 40 dB. The LC filter's quality factor is adjustable via SQUID parametric pumping, enabling power dissipation limits up to $\mu$W across a 100 MHz frequency band. The paper details the design methodology, presents experimental results, and evaluates the device's performance.

This study examines the epidemic progression of COVID-19 under the extreme assumption that acquired immunity is completely absent. Under this premise, the model reduces to the SIR framework, which is further simplified by replacing the standard population with a normalized version. This normalization facilitates the derivation of an analytical solution for $S(t)$, which is subsequently employed to calculate the time-dependent course of the outbreak. The results indicate that this closed-form solution aligns closely with empirical data from the initial phase of the pandemic, particularly in Italy, and the United States.

This study examines the impact of context selection on word embedding techniques. We introduce a new algorithm that automatically selects context windows, outperforming even manually defined maximum sizes. The method demonstrates that maximum distances of 10 and 20 for the words "NLP" and "Python," respectively, yield superior results compared to traditional methods. The research highlights that context window selection is a critical yet often overlooked factor in word embedding research. The proposed algorithm provides a straightforward solution to this challenge.

This work examines the maximal clique number in high-density random geometric graphs where edge probabilities approach one. We establish a lower bound for the clique number that matches the upper bound derived by Alon et al. (2015) for the related Erdős–Rényi random graph model. Furthermore, we investigate the $k$-clique number, demonstrating that the expected size of the maximal $k$-clique group is tightly bounded by a constant that is both independent of the graph's scale and nearly optimal relative to the limit of the largest complete subgraph.

We introduce a Lagrangian formulation for spinning stars, modeled as perfect fluids endowed with spin and spin-torsion coupling. This approach yields the corresponding Einstein field equations in a canonical form, suitable for deriving both the action and associated boundary terms. Additionally, our framework provides an expression for angular momentum, thereby extending previous work by Boyer and Lovelace.

This study analyzes the spherically symmetric Lemaître-Tolman-Bondi (LTB) solution within Palatini $f(R)$ gravity, formulated as $f(R)=R+\lambda R^2$. We demonstrate that this framework can be reduced to Einstein's equations involving an effective energy-momentum tensor. By treating the additional term as a perfect fluid, we derive its specific energy density and pressure profiles. Furthermore, we examine the fluid's thermodynamic characteristics, including its speed of sound and corresponding adiabatic index.

Quantum nonlocality, a cornerstone of quantum information theory, is typically demonstrated through the violation of Bell-type inequalities. However, experimental verification of this phenomenon is hindered by the fragility of quantum states against environmental noise, which can obscure nonlocal correlations. This study introduces a robust form of quantum nonlocality applicable to $N$-partite systems, observable via intensity measurements alone, without the need for specific local bases or complex state preparations. We derive Bell-type inequalities for $N$-partite contexts and prove that our proposed metric effectively captures quantum nonlocality even in $N$-qubit product states. Furthermore, we show that this approach withstands significant experimental noise, rendering it suitable for practical applications.

Visual attention serves as a critical indicator of user engagement with digital content. By analyzing web users' visual focus, we can derive insights into their interactions with web pages, thereby enhancing the design of engaging user interfaces. This study introduces a novel approach to forecasting gaze patterns over a short temporal window, utilizing features derived from recent gaze history. Our method employs a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network to process these features, achieving a 70% prediction accuracy for 1-second intervals.

The reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has emerged as a pivotal technology for enhancing wireless connectivity and spectral efficiency in future 6G networks. While existing research predominantly focuses on reflective RIS, which reflects incident signals back toward the source, this study introduces a novel transmissive RIS (tRIS) architecture designed to transmit incident signals past the surface. This innovation enables simultaneous connectivity enhancement and interference mitigation, a capability absent in reflective RIS. The paper details the design and prototyping of a tRIS unit operating at 2.4 GHz, which integrates a dual-mode antenna, a phase shifter, and a switch. The prototype's performance was validated through experimental demonstrations, including the creation of a transmissive RIS array. These findings confirm that the proposed tRIS technology holds significant promise for advancing wireless networks in the coming decades.

Offline reinforcement learning (RL) involves making decisions within a fixed dataset without further interaction with the environment. While recent advances in RL have achieved promising results, the majority of these advances rely on the assumption that the function approximator is linear. This paper investigates whether such linear structures can be maintained for nonlinear function approximators. We demonstrate that three prominent offline RL frameworks—those proposed by (i) Aslam et al. (2020), (ii) Fu et al. (2019), and (iii) Fu et al. (2018)—retain this linear structure even when utilizing nonlinear function approximators. Consequently, we derive new minimax-optimal regret bounds for these three settings by leveraging this property. Our methodology is straightforward and adaptable to other offline RL algorithms.

We demonstrate that the homotopy type of a simplicial set can be constructed using a specific category of endomorphisms for its constituent simplices, relying entirely on techniques involving only non-invertible morphisms, and, consequently, without employing any formal notion of homotopy in the process.

This paper examines planar three-body configurations where bodies form a collinear set. We analyze specific configurations involving two binary pairs sharing one body and a third isolated pair, focusing on the binary setup. We demonstrate that for any such arrangement, a periodic orbit exists.

Fluorescence Lifetime Imaging Microscopy (FLIM) is a powerful, non-invasive technique that measures the fluorescence lifetime of fluorophores, which serves as a crucial indicator of the local chemical environment. This review details the fundamental principles of FLIM, along with its advantages and limitations, and outlines various deconvolution methods designed to enhance spatial resolution. The text further presents a novel hybrid approach combining the regularized iterative method (RIM) with the alternating least squares (ALS) technique, demonstrating that this hybrid model significantly outperforms existing algorithms.

Product search is a fundamental component of e-commerce, and customizing search results to individual user preferences is crucial for enhancing user experience. This study introduces a Graph Convolution-based model designed to predict user actions within search results, enabling the creation of personalized rankings. The proposed approach models user behavior as a graph where nodes represent users, products, and search queries, and edges capture interactions between them. By utilizing graph convolution, the system generates embeddings for each node, which are then fed into a multi-layer perceptron to forecast user actions. The model's effectiveness is validated through evaluations on two real-world datasets.

This study introduces a new approach to graph embedding that relies on a neural network to approximate the manifold of the graph. The core methodology involves training the network to minimize the discrepancy between the input graph and the manifold, thereby deriving node embeddings from the output of this trained model. The proposed algorithm is designed to handle both labeled and unlabeled graphs, offering a unified framework for graph clustering and graph representation learning. Theoretical analysis confirms that the method achieves near-optimal performance, and extensive experiments on various real-world datasets demonstrate significant improvements in both clustering and representation tasks compared to current state-of-the-art solutions.

This study introduces a two-phase genetic algorithm designed to optimize non-orthogonal sequences for grant-free massive access scenarios. The initial phase employs genetic algorithms to generate candidate sequences, while the subsequent phase refines these candidates to minimize the maximum correlation coefficient. Numerical results demonstrate that this proposed method yields superior performance compared to existing state-of-the-art techniques.

Domain adaptation seeks to enhance the performance of a model trained on a source domain when applied to a distinct target domain. While adversarial approaches are effective at aligning source and target distributions, they often fail to handle the natural variability found within individual domains. To address this limitation, we introduce a novel framework that integrates adversarial learning with stochastic transformations. This method leverages domain adaptation to address intra-domain variations, thereby boosting robustness. Furthermore, we develop a new technique for generating synthetic target data, which further strengthens generalization capabilities. Comprehensive experiments on various cross-domain classification tasks demonstrate that our approach yields state-of-the-art results.

This paper establishes that all 2-local inner derivations on the Jordan matrix algebra $M_{n}(R)$, where $R$ is a commutative involutive ring, coincide exactly with the standard linear derivations on $M_{n}(R)$. Furthermore, it investigates linear derivations on the Jordan algebra $M_{n}(R)$ of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $R$ that vanish on a specific subset of $n-2$ diagonal elements.

This study examines how gravity affects the Dirac zero-angle phase, specifically focusing on the gravitational lensing of the Dirac monopole within the context of the Aharonov-Bohm effect. We find that the presence of a black hole induces an additional contribution to this phase shift, which is proportional to the mass of the black hole.

This study examines the existence of compact solitons within two-component Bose-Einstein condensates (BECs) featuring intercomponent interactions. We demonstrate that when these interactions are sufficiently strong, compact solitons can form, with their spatial dimensions determined by the interaction strength. Furthermore, we investigate the stability of these solitons regarding mass and spin-orbit coupling, showing that spin-orbit effects can induce a phase transition from a stable to an unstable state. Additionally, we analyze the influence of spin-orbit coupling on the soliton's mass, revealing a linear dependence of the mass on the spin-orbit parameter.

The $\Lambda_c(2595)^+$, which decays into $D^0\pi^-$, and the $\Lambda_c(2625)^+$, which decays into $D^+\pi^-$, are both candidates for excited states of the ground-state $\Lambda_c^+$ baryon. These two states exhibit a mass splitting of approximately 30 MeV and possess opposite $J^P$ assignments of $1/2^-$ and $5/2^+$. This mass splitting is consistent with the prediction of the massive quark spin symmetry (MQSS) for the MQSS doublet formed by the $1s1/2$ and $2s1/2$ configurations of the $cqq$ system. However, the decay modes of these states contradict MQSS expectations: the $D^0\pi^-$ channel is suppressed relative to the $D^+\pi^-$ channel, whereas the MQSS predicts the opposite. This work investigates whether the MQSS doublet hypothesis can be reconciled with the observed decay patterns. We demonstrate that the MQSS predicts a suppression of the $D^0\pi^-$ partial width relative to the $D^+\pi^-$ width, provided the MQSS parameter $\alpha$ is sufficiently small. Consequently, the MQSS framework can be reconciled with the decay data if $\alpha \lesssim 0.1$.

This work investigates the extension of continuous functions defined on orbit spaces, where the original functions are liftable to continuous functions on the underlying total spaces. We establish that such functions can be approximated by "smooth" liftable functions, provided the group action is locally linear. Furthermore, we demonstrate that these functions are not dense within the space of liftable continuous functions. Finally, we provide an example involving the action of a finite group on a manifold, where the restriction maps from the manifold to the manifold's quotient space are neither injective nor surjective.

This white paper outlines the potential of future high-energy muon colliders to probe the properties of axion-like particles (ALPs) and similar entities. These particles are currently favored candidates for dark matter and are extensively investigated due to their capacity to resolve the strong CP problem. By leveraging the distinctive characteristics of upcoming muon colliders, we outline a comprehensive search strategy for ALPs across a broad spectrum of masses and coupling constants. We detail how muon colliders can uniquely access parameter spaces that are out of reach for the LHC and the HL-LHC, while also highlighting the specific physics reach of this proposed muon collider program.

The growing complexity of modern systems, driven by the need to manage vast data volumes and support diverse workloads, has made metadata a critical resource for optimizing system performance. This paper introduces MetaSys, a comprehensive open-source metadata management platform designed to facilitate cross-layer system optimizations. By utilizing a knowledge graph, MetaSys enables the storage, analysis, and assessment of metadata across various system layers. We highlight MetaSys's flexibility and extensibility through its implementation in two distinct case studies: first, a database optimization framework that leverages metadata to enhance query performance, and second, a system architecture for automatically generating metadata-driven workloads. These studies demonstrate MetaSys's practical value in real-world scenarios. Finally, the paper outlines the project's future roadmap, which includes plans to expand the system's capabilities and broaden its application scope.

This study introduces transfer learning approaches for image classification that leverage artificial data and Siamese networks. The paper details two specific methods: the first employs a data augmentation technique using a Siamese network to generate artificial training samples, while the second utilizes a Siamese network directly to classify new images by comparing them against existing training data. Both techniques were evaluated on the CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 datasets. Experimental results indicate that these proposed methods yield performance comparable to standard transfer learning and surpass classification based on random initialization.

This paper examines a class of $N$-dimensional quasilinear elliptic systems with both convolution and decaying terms, where the latter are coupled with a specified steady-state 3-vector field. We establish the existence of unique positive solutions that decay at infinity, along with their corresponding principal eigenfunctions. The analysis relies on a fixed-point argument, complemented by the application of the maximum principle and relevant comparison theorems.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) have proven highly effective for sequential data tasks, such as language modeling and speech recognition. However, their ability to capture long-term dependencies is constrained by vanishing gradients. This paper introduces Fourier Recurrent Units (FRUs), a novel architecture designed to overcome this limitation. By leveraging Fourier series to model temporal dynamics, FRUs can theoretically store information over arbitrarily long sequences. Empirical evaluations on both language modeling and speech recognition demonstrate that FRUs significantly outperform standard RNN variants in handling long-term dependencies.

This paper introduces a new Markov decision process (MDM) framework designed to identify an optimal policy, which is particularly useful for navigation and search tasks. The framework is constructed by embedding a target state within the MDP, creating a guaranteed path to that state. This approach enables the derivation of an optimal policy leading to the target. The study presents a method for calculating such a policy and provides a method for determining the policy's cost. The paper further analyzes the computational complexity of these operations. The proposed framework is then applied to solve a navigation problem, demonstrating its effectiveness. The paper concludes with a discussion of the framework's potential applications. We introduce a novel method for generating high-brightness, linearly polarized attosecond electron bunchs utilizing dual-wake injection. This approach employs a two-stage plasma wakefield accelerator driven by a single laser pulse, where the initial wakefield creates a seed bunch and the subsequent wakefield accelerates it to high energies. The compactness of the setup, achieved through the use of a single laser, combined with the injection of an electron bunch lasting only 100 attoseconds, results in an electron beam characterized by an ultrahigh brightness. Furthermore, the transverse electron motion is governed by the linear polarization of the laser, enabling precise control over the beam's polarization state.

This review examines the evolution of complexity from an astronomical viewpoint, focusing on how complexity is measured and defined. We begin by exploring the origins of life, covering the formation of the universe, the conditions for life, and the chemical processes leading to biological emergence. We then analyze how complexity increases throughout stellar and planetary formation, alongside the geological and biological drivers of this trend within the solar system. Finally, we address the future trajectory of complexity, considering factors such as technological advancement and space colonization.

Climate change research is expanding rapidly, creating a critical need for evidence-based policy formulation. This study examines the advantages and limitations of utilizing open-source repositories and artificial intelligence to map the current state of climate alteration research, specifically focusing on identifying gaps in knowledge and pinpointing promising areas for future development. The analysis reveals that while open repositories offer a wealth of data, they are often plagued by poor quality control, resulting in inconsistent metadata and incomplete metadata structures. Consequently, AI-driven mapping of open repositories is prone to significant biases, which can distort the resulting research landscape. Furthermore, the authors demonstrate that AI can effectively identify specific research gaps and promising directions, but these insights must be interpreted with caution to avoid reinforcing existing biases. Ultimately, the paper concludes that while AI is a powerful tool for mapping climate change research, it must be used in conjunction with other methods to ensure robust and equitable policy formulation.

Android, as a platform built on Linux, is susceptible to side-channel attacks that exploit the interaction between software and hardware. The Android Native Development Kit (NDK) enables the integration of native C/C++ code within Android applications, thereby expanding the attack surface for such vulnerabilities. This study examines the NDK to identify side-channel risks, proposing a semi-automated framework named ASVAAN that combines static analysis with machine learning to pinpoint vulnerable functions. By utilizing a dataset of 1,000 C/C++ functions, we trained a model to forecast which functions are likely to exhibit side-channel behaviors. Preliminary evaluations indicate that ASVAAN successfully identifies vulnerable functions with 90% accuracy.

This paper presents a methodology for analyzing the temporal evolution of ego networks associated with self-labeled individual nodes within the Ethereum blockchain. By utilizing transaction data, we construct ego networks where the individual of interest serves as the central node, and connections are defined by transactions involving the individual and their immediate neighbors. To facilitate this, we developed a Python-based tool that extracts and processes blockchain data, followed by the generation of time-series ego networks for distinct individuals. The study then examines the topological and structural dynamics of these networks over time.

This work explores the relationship between bichordal (BV) and pomset calculi, which are interaction models for linear logic. We demonstrate that these systems are semantically equivalent by constructing a translation from pomset calculus to BV that preserves exponential exponentiality. This translation maps the exponential modality into a new interaction-specific operator, termed "parallel," which is grounded in the parallel composition of proofs. This approach yields a streamlined translation of pomset calculus that eliminates the need for complex cut-elimination procedures. Consequently, we derive a direct and elementary equivalence between the pbc fragment and the pomset fragment lacking exponential features.

We demonstrate that the $n$-point polygon operator $\mu_n$ defined within the context of the Ding-Iohara-Miki algebra possesses a closed-form expression. This formula is formulated using the $q$-binomial theorem and the $q$-hypergeometric series framework.

We present photometric redshifts for 12,000 galaxies located in the W-CDF-S and ELAIS-S1 fields, derived from WFC3/IR imaging data spanning 0.36 to 4.5 microns. These photometric redshifts were generated using the EAZY code, which fits the spectral energy distributions of the galaxies with a combination of galaxy templates. The photometric redshifts were cross-verified against spectroscopic redshifts from the SDSS and VVDS surveys, yielding a median scatter of 0.014 and a mean offset of 0.001. The photometric redshifts are accurate to within 0.014 for galaxies with $z > 0.5$ and within 0.02 for galaxies with $z < 0.5$.

This paper introduces a novel Bayesian Decision Support System (DASS) designed to aid energy system strategy formulation. The system integrates a comprehensive database of historical energy statistics with complex mathematical models to generate probabilistic forecasts regarding the impacts of specific policy interventions. By utilizing these forecasted outcomes, the models calculate the anticipated benefits of various strategies, enabling the identification of the most effective policy options. The authors detail the development of this DASS, highlighting its key components, including a database management framework, a statistical model for forecasting energy consumption and emissions, and a decision-making algorithm. Furthermore, the paper demonstrates the system's practical application by evaluating the potential outcomes of two distinct policy strategies.

The electronic wavefunction is characterized by a complex entanglement structure that is critical for developing efficient methods to simulate it. This study demonstrates that the two-electron wavefunction can be represented as a matrix product state (MPS) with a tensor bond index of three. This specific bond dimension of three is both necessary and sufficient, and it is achieved by enforcing the Pauli exclusion principle for spatial wavefunctions through the inclusion of spin. This result is significant for simulating electronic structures using MPS-based techniques, as it allows for the efficient handling of two-electron integrals.

We introduce a minimal framework featuring a new weakly interacting massive vector boson, $\mathbf{X}$, which couples to leptons. This interaction offers a solution to the long-standing $g-2$ anomaly by accounting for discrepancies in both the muon and tau lepton anomalous magnetic moments. The model successfully reconciles these predictions with current experimental constraints, notably the $\tau \to \mu \gamma$ decay limit, by suggesting a mass for the $\mathbf{X}$ boson exceeding 1 TeV.

The surge in coastal flooding driven by climate change and population growth has created an urgent need for rapid, accurate, and reliable flood prediction tools. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing neural operators to create a surrogate model for simulating coastal flooding. This method is grounded in the Navier-Stokes equations, which govern fluid dynamics, and incorporates essential physical principles, including the no-slip boundary condition and the moving free surface. The model's efficacy was validated using a 2D hydrodynamic model of the North Sea, specifically focusing on the North Sea coast of the Netherlands. The results demonstrate that the proposed method can accurately forecast coastal flooding with a computational speed exceeding 100,000 times that of the original hydrodynamic model.

The BeyondPlanck initiative, a comprehensive analysis of all available cosmological datasets, culminated in a series of 17 workshops held between 2015 and 2016. These events were designed to foster collaboration and address the challenges of merging data from various sources. This document outlines the BeyondPlanck project's approach to data sharing, emphasizing its commitment to open data dissemination, reproducibility, and long-term data preservation. It details the project's data infrastructure, software tools, and workflows, and outlines the specific strategies employed to ensure the data remains accessible and usable for the foreseeable future.

This study examines a reaction-diffusion system composed of coupled reaction-diffusion networks connected via a transmission mechanism. While prior research has established that the Turing instability of such transmittable systems is governed by the transmission's eigenvalues, this paper demonstrates that the pattern formation is further regulated by the system's boundary conditions. Specifically, we show that the transmission eigenvalues are augmented by additional eigenvalues derived from the boundary constraints. Furthermore, we reveal that the Turing instability persists even when the transmission eigenvalues remain stable, provided the boundary eigenvalues exhibit instability. Numerical simulations confirm that these boundary-driven eigenvalues significantly influence the resulting Turing patterns.

Quantum wires (1D nanostructures) are fundamental to nanophotonics, yet their optical properties remain difficult to predict due to the complex interplay between quantum confinement and material characteristics. This study presents a theoretical and experimental investigation of the polarization anisotries in single wires of bulk GaN wurtzite crystals. We demonstrate that the polarization anisotries in quantum wires are primarily governed by the material's crystal symmetry rather than the wire's geometry. Specifically, our findings indicate that the energy gap between the in-plane and out-of-plane excitonic transitions in wurtzite quantum wires is significantly larger than in conventional quantum dots or quantum wells. This substantial energy separation is attributed to the unique electronic band structure of bulk wurtzite crystals, which exhibits a large polarization-dependent effective mass difference between in-plane and out-of-plane directions. These results are expected to advance the development of novel devices, such as polariton lasers, utilizing quantum wires fabricated from bulk wurtzite crystals.

Negotiation dialogue systems (NDS) are designed to interact with adversaries who aim to maximize their own utility while minimizing that of the system. Although adversarial strategies are typically represented using out-of-the-dataset data, this data often fails to capture the true nature of real-world adversaries, leading to suboptimal NDS performance. To address this, we introduce a two-stage training approach for NDS that leverages associated data to refine out-of-the-dataset adversarial modeling. Specifically, we employ a two-stage training protocol: the NDS is first trained on out-of-the-dataset data, and subsequently fine-tuned using associated data. This fine-tuning process is guided by an adversarial model that concurrently updates the NDS and itself to simulate a more realistic adversary. This joint optimization ensures the adversarial model remains aligned with the evolving capabilities of the NDS. Furthermore, we utilize a self-supervised learning method to modify associated data, generating adjustments that reflect the NDS's current performance and better approximate real-world adversary behavior. Experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly outperforms current state-of-the-art methods across all metrics.

This study examines a four-dimensional effective theory derived from compactifying a ten-dimensional light-like slice segment of type II superstring theory, where this segment corresponds to a D8-brane. The resulting framework features a time-dependent string tension, establishing a clear link between the tension and the ten-dimensional dilaton field. We analyze the cosmological solutions within this four-dimensional context and investigate how the string tension influences the evolution of a universe dominated by matter.

This study addresses the sequential allocation of $N$ agents to $M$ locations, where $N$ significantly exceeds $M$. The objective is to minimize the total cost of assignments, defined as the sum of pairwise costs between agents and locations. We introduce a two-stage approach: the first stage involves a greedy assignment that prioritizes balancing the count of agents per location; the second stage optimizes the final assignment given these counts. We analyze the performance of this method against the optimal solution, deriving a theoretical upper bound for the cost ratio. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the method achieves the optimal theoretical bound for the cost ratio among all algorithms that adhere to a specific structural property.

This study introduces a novel, unified dataset covering the global container shipping industry from 1966 to 2020, comprising freight rates, shipping volumes, newbuilding orders, second-hand transactions, and scrap prices. This comprehensive collection is the first to integrate freight rate and volume data with newbuilding and second-hand metrics, thereby enabling more robust analysis of the industry's long-term dynamics. The newly compiled dataset is available for download at https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/forthcoming.

Online anomaly detection is a critical component of numerous machine learning workflows, particularly in computer vision, where it serves to filter out defective training data and mitigate performance degradation caused by noisy inputs. This work presents a comprehensive meta-analysis of anomaly detection methodologies, evaluating their strengths and weaknesses through a comparative study of 14 distinct sensors across 11 datasets. We introduce a novel dataset comprising 11 anomaly examples, expanding the collective dataset pool to 16. Our findings indicate that while certain sensors excel in specific scenarios, no single approach consistently outperforms others across all situations. Consequently, we propose a new sensor that leverages the strengths of existing methods to surpass them in the majority of test cases.

This study presents a novel approach for segmenting gliomas in brain MRI images by leveraging deep learning, specifically convolutional neural networks (CNNs). The methodology involves training a CNN on a dataset of 100 manually annotated MRI scans, followed by a prediction phase applied to 50 new images. To address the common issue of false positives, a post-processing technique was introduced that employs a support vector machine (SVM) to filter out erroneous predictions. The system's performance was evaluated using the F1-score, Dice coefficient, and mean absolute error (MAE). The results demonstrate that the proposed post-processing method effectively reduces false positives without compromising the integrity of the predicted tumor regions.

This paper introduces the notions of statistical convergence for sequences ordered by directed sets. It defines the concepts of statistically bounded and convergent sequences through these directed sets and investigates their fundamental properties while highlighting the application of this method to the natural numbers as an example.

This study introduces a non-continuous Galerkin finite element approach for solving Rosenau's equation, utilizing a finite-time step method for time integration. The proposed numerical framework is rigorously analyzed to establish both existence and uniqueness of solutions, alongside proofs of uniform error bounds in the $L^2$ norm. Furthermore, computational experiments are conducted to substantiate the theoretical findings and to evaluate the method's efficiency across different implementations.

This paper investigates the well-posedness of a coupled partial differential equation (PDE) system modeling the Navier-Stokes equations for a compressible fluid coupled with an elastic membrane. The analysis establishes the existence of a unique mild solution defined on a suitable interval of time. The core of our approach involves demonstrating the validity of an $\alpha$-inf-sup condition for the system's associated operator pair, a criterion known to be both necessary and sufficient for the existence of a unique mild solution.

We report the successful creation of charged interlayer excitons (ILEs) in van der Waals heterostructures, specifically MoSe2/WSe2, using a high-intensity magnetic field. Our observations indicate that these ILEs form a Wigner crystal (WCr) at low temperatures, a state that persists up to room temperature under strong magnetic fields. This WCr formation is confirmed by the emergence of a series of equally spaced sidebands in the ILE optical transition, a phenomenon attributed to the periodic modulation of the exciton's dipole moment. Furthermore, we observe a magnetic field-induced transition from a liquid to a WCr within the ILE system. This phase shift is evidenced by the evolution of the optical transition from a Lorentzian to a sharp delta-like peak, accompanied by the disappearance of the sidebands. This transition is driven by the magnetic field's ability to suppress the kinetic energy of the excitons, thereby facilitating Wigner crystallization.

This paper introduces an ideal accelerated degradation test (AIDT) framework based on a bivariate gamma process incorporating relational elements. The proposed method offers a more robust approach for assessing the reliability of new products by utilizing a gamma process with relational attributes to model degradation trajectories. The study derives the maximum likelihood estimators (MLEs) for model parameters, the conditional mean-squared error (MSE) of the estimators, and the reliability function. Additionally, the paper provides the asymptotic distribution of the MLEs and the reliability function. Simulation results demonstrate that the estimators derived in this work exhibit superior performance compared to existing methods. Finally, the paper applies this methodology to analyze the lifetime degradation of a battery system.

We have analyzed the triangular flow ($v_3$) in Au+Au and Cu+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 200 GeV using the AMPT model, which incorporates a multiphase transport approach. Our results indicate that the $v_3$ values for charged particles and identified hadrons (specifically pions, kaons, and protons) align well with experimental data. Furthermore, we examined the $v_3$ dependence on the number of participating nucleons and found that the model's predictions for this trend are in good agreement with the data. Finally, we calculated the elliptic subevent method for determining $v_3$ and confirmed that it yields results consistent with those obtained from the event-plane method.

The polytropic index ($\gamma$) serves as a critical parameter for characterizing the thermodynamic state of solar wind plasma. This study investigates the polytropic properties of plasma within the interaction region formed between high-speed solar wind streams (HSS) and interplanetary coronal mass ejections (ICMEs). By analyzing data from the STEREO-A and STEREO-B spacecraft, we examined the plasma dynamics in the interaction zones created when HSS encounters occurred with ICMEs from both space observatories. Our results indicate that the polytropic index in these interaction regions is consistently lower than that of the background solar wind. Furthermore, we observed that the polytropic index in these regions is significantly lower for STEREO-A compared to STEREO-B. This discrepancy is attributed to the specific configuration of the ICME-HSS interaction, which is more pronounced at STEREO-A. Consequently, we conclude that the plasma in the interaction region exhibits a more "isothermal" behavior than in the background solar wind, a condition that is particularly evident at STEREO-A.

This paper examines the Random Waypoint movement model, a widely adopted method for simulating mobile entities in wireless ad-hoc and mobile networks. We establish the model's mathematical foundations, analyze its probabilistic properties, and demonstrate its connection to Poisson processes. Furthermore, we derive closed-form expressions for the probability density functions of path length and travel time, and prove that path lengths adhere to a Pareto distribution.
