This study introduces a novel framework for refining atomic structures using a conditional diffusion model trained on molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. This approach is designed to address the significant noise present in diffraction patterns from atom probe tomography (APT). The model's effectiveness is demonstrated on a binary alloy, where it successfully recovers atomic configurations from noisy experimental data. Furthermore, we evaluate the model's capacity to identify atomic structures from simulated APT data that have undergone additional noise corruption.

This study introduces Lagrangian instruments designed to measure oceanic transport and mixing, a concept that unifies the concepts of Lagrangian and Eulerian observations. By applying a time-dependent coordinate transformation, the instruments directly quantify the kinematic attributes of fluid parcels, specifically the divergence and stretching of material lines. A prototype of these instruments is currently under development, and the paper also presents a theoretical model of the ocean as a passive tracer flow to validate the utility of this approach.

The Equation of State (EOS) and Entropy (ES) method are employed to investigate the thermodynamic scaling behavior of polymeric glass-forming liquids. By utilizing the scaling framework to analyze isobaric specific heat ($C_p$) and isothermal compressibility ($\kappa_T$), we demonstrate that these properties collapse onto a single universal curve across a wide spectrum of polymers, including polystyrene, poly(methyl methacrylate), and poly(ethylene glycol). This universal trend persists regardless of variations in molecular weight, chemical composition, or chain flexibility. Furthermore, we establish that the correlation length ($\xi$) is linearly proportional to the square root of the isobaric specific heat ($C_p$). This finding supports the hypothesis that the scaling exponent $\omega$ equals 0.5, consistent with the Adam-Gibbs theory.

This paper investigates the semi-discretization of a modified Camassa-Holm equation that incorporates a linear dispersion term, achieved by combining a semi-discrete method with the continuous Longuet-Higgins and Mizuno approach. We establish the Bäcklund transformation and the auto-backlund transformation for this system, both expressed via a semi-discrete framework. Furthermore, we derive the Miwa transformation connecting the semi-discrete and continuous forms and utilize it to establish the integrability of the semi-discrete altered Camassa-Holm equation with linear dispersion using the Hirota technique.

This paper introduces a quantum field theory framework for extended de Broglie-Bohm - Bell quantum mechanics, where the wavefunction is defined as a twisted field. This twisted nature arises from the wavefunction's dependence on both particle positions and specific internal symmetries. The theory demonstrates that the fundamental non-relativistic quantum commutation relations emerge naturally from the commutation of fields twisted in this manner. Additionally, the work explores contextuality, analyzing how it manifests within the theory.

This study examines the secular evolution of the spin and quadrupole moments of precessing compact binaries, which are driven by the Lense-Thirring effect. We analyze the long-term behavior of the spin and quadrupole vectors for systems comprising black holes, gravastars, neutron stars, and boson stars, as well as their orbital parameters. Our findings indicate that the secular evolution of the spin and quadrupole moments is governed by the specific nature of the components, with the evolution timescale for the spin-quadrupole phase angle being inversely proportional to the orbital period. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the evolution of the spin and quadrupole moments is significantly influenced by the initial orbital phase angle, a factor that is often overlooked in previous literature.

YOLO (You're Only Live Once) stands as a leading real-time object detection framework. This paper presents YOLOv4, an enhanced iteration built upon YOLOv3, which integrates cutting-edge techniques to substantially boost both inference speed and accuracy. This new version offers a real-time capability of 60 frames per second (fps) on a single NVIDIA Titan Xp GPU, delivering a 28% performance uplift compared to YOLOv3. Furthermore, YOLOv4 surpasses the state-of-the-art single-stage detectors, including SSD and Faster R-CNN, across multiple metrics. The source code and pre-trained models are accessible at https://github.com/ultralytics/yolov4.

This document details the revision of the Minho Citation Resource (MCR), a comprehensive collection of metadata covering citations, citing papers, and cited‑for‑reference papers from 1900 to 2020. Drawing on Web of Science and Scopus databases, the MCR offers a broad scope of scientific literature. This update expands the dataset to include records from 2020, introduces refined author name disambiguation, and enhances citation matching through the incorporation of additional data sources.

Concept lattices have been widely employed in machine learning for clustering and classification, particularly in scenarios where attributes are either binary or categorical. In contrast, decision trees excel in contexts where attributes are ordered and numeric. This paper introduces the adaptation of concept lattices for the construction of decision trees, alongside an investigation into the potential synergy between these structures and random forests.

Machine learning (ML) systems are increasingly integrated into critical societal domains, necessitating a rigorous evaluation of their performance. Yet, assessing these systems is complex, often requiring multiple tests across diverse datasets and metrics. This study examines the assessment practices of researchers and practitioners by analyzing 1,000 papers from the top-tier venues ICML, NeurIPS, and ICASSP. Our findings reveal that ML work frequently undergoes limited assessment, with many studies relying on a single dataset and metric. Furthermore, there is a significant mismatch between what different evaluators deem essential; researchers tend to prioritize different assessments than those considered crucial by their peers or industry practitioners. These results underscore the urgent need for standardized assessment protocols to ensure the reliable deployment of ML systems in real-world contexts.

The challenge of identifying anomalies within data is a longstanding issue in machine learning. While many existing methods focus on detecting deviations from known distributions, our research investigates a distinct scenario: identifying rare classes that are present in the data but currently lack labels. We term this the "rare-class identification" problem. We demonstrate that current approaches, which typically assume anomalies are absent from the training set, fail to perform adequately when the training data contains rare instances of the target categories. Consequently, we introduce a new framework for Rare-Class Identification (RCI) that leverages the concept of "new categories." This approach utilizes a multi-stage process to detect novel subcategories within the data, subsequently synthesizing them into a unified category that represents the rare class. We validate this approach using three real-world datasets, showing that it outperforms existing anomaly detection methods.

The objective of this study is to develop a robust method for extracting local atomic structure from focused-probe ptychography data of thick samples. We demonstrate that a straightforward linearization approach, which assumes a linear relationship between the probe-induced phase shift and the exit-wave phase shift, fails to capture the intricate phase shifts occurring in thick specimens. Consequently, this limitation results in significant errors in the reconstructed phase shifts. To address this, we introduce a nonlinear pipeline that effectively determines local atomic structure. This new pipeline incorporates a nonlinear phase shift model, a robust phase-retrieval algorithm, and a deconvolution method to mitigate the impact of the probe's nonlinear phase shift. We validate this approach using both simulations and experimental data from focused-probe ptychography of a thick Si(111) sample. The results show that the proposed pipeline successfully overcomes contrast inversions and accurately resolves local atomic structure, even when the probe exhibits strong nonlinear phase shifts.

This work examines the asymptotic current operator $J^{\mu}$, which is a central element in the study of the thermodynamic properties of nonequilibrium states within many-body systems. We demonstrate that $J^{\mu}$ remains gauge-invariant in any $d$-dimensional setting, provided it is constructed from the $d$-component spinor field $\psi$ and its conjugate $\psi^{\dagger}$, alongside the $d \times d$ matrix of random first-order differential operators acting on these spinors. This random operator framework is defined by a $d$-component vector of random functions, $\nabla\phi$, representing the gradient of a scalar field. Furthermore, we establish that the current's asymptotic behavior is fully determined by the large-scale characteristics of $\nabla\phi$.

Recurrent neural networks (RNNs) are extensively utilized in machine learning to model time-series data. However, their training is hindered by the "vanishing gradient" problem, which complicates the learning of long-term dependencies. Recently, researchers have introduced bio-inspired reservoir computing (RC) as a promising alternative to RNNs. This approach effectively mitigates the vanishing gradient issue and simplifies the training process, making it particularly suitable for real-time applications. This study investigates the learning capabilities of RNNs and RC networks by examining how their topological structures influence training dynamics. We demonstrate that the learning performance of RC networks is significantly more sensitive to reservoir topology than that of RNNs. Furthermore, we identify a critical threshold for the reservoir's path length, beyond which learning performance degrades sharply. These findings offer valuable insights for designing reservoir computing systems tailored to specific tasks.

This study examines the evolution of three interacting bosons within a harmonic trap, focusing on the effects of interatomic interactions. We specifically investigate the three-body binding energies and scattering lengths associated with Efimov states, demonstrating that these quantities are highly sensitive to the trap's anisotropy. Furthermore, we analyze how the system's behavior changes when the number of available bound states transitions from zero to one or two, revealing that this quench process is highly anisotropic.

Quantum kernel methods have recently gained significant traction in quantum machine learning, offering a framework to analyze the kernel representation of data. However, existing techniques for kernel estimation are often inefficient, as they necessitate repeated measurements of numerous outcomes. This paper introduces a novel kernel estimation method leveraging Hong-Ou-Mandel (HOM) interference between photons from two quantum circuits. Our approach demonstrates that estimating a kernel element requires only a single measurement of a photon pair, regardless of the number of input features. We further provide a theoretical proof that our method can recover the exact quantum kernel. Additionally, we show that our technique surpasses conventional methods by enabling kernel estimation with lower measurement error and fewer resources.

This paper introduces a novel algorithm for the rapid and precise evaluation of the Newtonian potential on planar domains, leveraging properties of the error function. We demonstrate that the potential can be reduced to an error function integral, which is further expressed via a series expansion. This approach allows for the derivation of a computationally efficient, high-precision formula for the potential. We also establish a theoretical error bound for the approximation method and validate the theory with numerical examples.
